title: Light and Electromagnetic Radiation
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Light and Electromagnetic Radiation Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Energy can be transferred as both a particle and a wave: the electromagnetic spectrum, properties of light (reflection, refraction, absorption), mirrors and lenses, and how the eye sees. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 8, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets (BC): the electromagnetic spectrum, reflection, refraction, colour, lenses and how we see. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Light is one part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
key_sub: Light reflects, refracts and is absorbed.
body_html:
How to think about it

Electromagnetic radiation includes radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays. They all travel at the speed of light but have different wavelengths and energy.

Light travels in straight lines. It reflects off mirrors (angle of incidence = angle of reflection), refracts (bends) when it passes from one material to another, and is absorbed by dark objects. Lenses bend light to form images, as in the eye, cameras and microscopes.

Example

A ray hits a mirror at 30°. What is the angle of reflection?

They are equal.

Answer: 30°

Example

Why does a straw look bent in water?

Light changes speed.

Answer: refraction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking we see by light leaving our eyes.
  • Thinking a red shirt is red because it absorbs red light (it reflects it).
  • Thinking radio waves are sound waves.

items.q: Which has the higher frequency: microwaves or X-rays?

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the normal is 25°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 25° (both measured from the normal).

items.q: The angle of incidence on a plane mirror is 35°. What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
items.e: The angle between them is i + r = 35° + 35° = 70°.

items.q: The angle of incidence on a plane mirror is 50°. What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
items.e: The angle between them is i + r = 50° + 50° = 100°.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 50° to the mirror surface. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of incidence = 90° − 50° = 40° (from the normal), so the angle of reflection is 40°.

items.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the mirror surface is 15°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angles are measured from the normal: 90° − 15° = 75°, and i = r.

items.e: Angles are measured from the normal: 90° − 70° = 20°, and i = r.

items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so the angle is 90° − 35° = 55°.

items.q: Why does a white sheet of paper look white to Liam in white sunlight?
c: It absorbs red light and reflects the other colours.
It absorbs all colours of light.
It makes its own coloured light.
It reflects all colours of light.
items.e: We see the colours an object reflects.

items.q: Kai's model: “A bike reflector shines back at a car's headlights.” Is the wave mainly reflected, absorbed or transmitted?
items.e: Waves can be reflected (bounce), absorbed (taken in, often as heat) or transmitted (pass through).

items.q: Emma shines a flashlight at clean water in a glass. What happens to the light?
c: It transmits almost all light, so you can see clearly through it.
It transmits no light; light is reflected or absorbed.
The light is turned into sound.
It transmits some light but scatters it, so things look blurry.
items.e: Clean water in a glass is transparent.

items.q: A ray of light leaves a glass block into air at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: Light travels at 1.97 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
The refractive index of glass is 1.5. What is the speed of light in glass? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
A ray enters glass (refractive index 1.5) from air and is refracted at 20° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.5 × sin 20°, so i = 30.9°.

items.q: Light travels at 1.24 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
Mateo notices: “A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is.” What explains this?
c: Light from the bottom bends as it leaves the water.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: Ethan notices: “A magnifying glass makes letters look bigger.” What explains this?
c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
The curved lens bends light rays toward each other.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 40° ÷ sin 25° = 1.52.

items.q: Lucas notices: “A fish in a pond is not exactly where it appears to be.” What explains this?

items.q: The refractive index of diamond is 2.42. What is the speed of light in diamond? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)

c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.

items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

What is the image in a camera or the eye like?
items.e: Real images can be focused on a screen or sensor.

items.q: A person who is far-sighted (hyperopia) needs which lens?
items.e: The focus is behind the retina; a converging lens moves it forward.

items.q: Two thin lenses of focal lengths 50 cm and −15 cm are placed in contact. What is the focal length of the combination?
Which part of the eye focuses light onto the retina?
c: the lens (with help from the cornea)
items.e: The cornea does most of the bending; the lens adjusts the focus.

items.q: What does the iris do?
c: it carries signals to the brain
it controls the size of the pupil and so how much light enters
items.e: In bright light the pupil gets smaller.

Why do optical fibres carry light around corners?
c: light reflects totally inside the fibre again and again
the fibre makes its own light
items.e: Total internal reflection traps the light in the core.

items.q: Which device uses a converging lens to make a real image on a sensor?
items.e: Like the eye, a camera focuses a real, inverted image.

items.q: What is the blind spot of the eye?
c: the coloured part of the eye
the place where the optic nerve leaves the retina, with no light receptors
items.e: We do not notice it because the brain fills in the gap.

items.q: Which device uses two converging lenses to see very small objects?
